passage:
"You've been quiet since the lab meeting. What happened?" Amandeep asked, dropping her bag on the hostel bed.
"Dr. Mehta gave the conference slot to Tanmay. His results are weaker. Everyone knows his cousin plays cricket with Dr. Mehta."
"Maybe there's a reason."
"Maybe. But my poster wasn't even mentioned. I used to copy how Dr. Mehta wrote problem statements. I thought everything about that was perfect."
"So are you going to tear up your notebook?"
"I almost did." Chandrika opened it and looked at the first page. "But the way of framing a question still works. That part is mine now, fair or not."
"And the slot?"
"I'll ask plainly why. And I won't decide that every professor is the same."

qa.q: What does Chandrika's remark about copying the problem statements suggest about how she felt before?
qa.a: She admired Dr. Mehta and thought everything about that work was perfect, so the letdown stings more.

qa.q: What could Chandrika do next about the conference slot?
qa.a: Ask Dr. Mehta plainly why Tanmay was chosen, while keeping the way of framing questions she learned.

qa.q: Why might Amandeep ask if she will tear up her notebook?
qa.a: Amandeep may worry that Chandrika will reject everything and everyone in authority, so the question checks that she is not throwing away useful learning.

grounding: A student finds her mentor biased, keeps what he taught and refuses to distrust all authority.
